newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece arrests woman in German disco bombing probe.
newsitem.headline: Greece arrests woman in German disco bombing probe.

text.p: Greek police arrested a German woman in connection with the bombing of a West Berlin disco in 1986 that killed three people and wounded 200, including many U.S. servicemen, police sources said on Saturday.
The woman, identified as Andrea Hasler, was arrested on Thursday night in Halkidiki near this northern port city.
Another German woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of planting the bomb.
The sources said Hasler, 31, was with her two-year-old son and a boyfriend when she was arrested at the request of German authorities.
They said she was taken to Diavata prison in Salonika and they expected extradition to move quickly because she faced no charges in Greece.
The woman and her companions entered Greece six days ago. The sources said it appeared only the woman was sought by the German authorities.
In Berlin, prosecutors said they had arrested a 37-year-old German woman, identified only as Verena C., and her Palestinian ex-husband, Ali C., on Thursday.

The United States blamed Libya for the attack on the "La Belle" disco and responded by bombing the Arab state, killing at least 15 people, including an adopted 15-month-old daughter of leader Muammar Gaddafi and wounding more than 100.
German prosecutors said they believed Verena C. had planted the bomb at the request of Ali C. and another suspect, Yasser Shraydi, who was extradited to Germany from Lebanon in May this year.

German authorities believe the attack was orchestrated from the Libyan embassy in East Berlin. They have also issued arrest warrants for three former members of the Libyan embassy in East Berlin -- identified only by the surnames Elamin, Keshlaf and Al Abani -- and a Libyan secret service member named Rashed.
The prosecutors believe those suspects provided the explosives and helped organise the bombing but that they are now back in their homeland.
Two U.S. soldiers and a Turkish woman were killed in the April 1986 attack on the club in Berlin's Schoeneberg district and scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel were injured.
